decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Gholdengo for immediate Tailwind/Helping Hand pressure and strong spread damage, while avoiding reliance on Whimsicott alone. Bring Mega Blastoise for Incineroar and Kingambit, plus Tauros for Intimidate and Fighting/Fire pressure; preserve Gholdengo around Kingambit’s Sucker Punch.
decisions.notebook: Opponent favors Incineroar Fake Out plus Parting Shot cycling, Mega Gardevoir Protect and repeated Hyper Voice, and Talonflame Tailwind. Kingambit has Protect and Sucker Punch; avoid leaving Gholdengo exposed. Prefer immediate pressure and layered speed control; Mega Blastoise answers Incineroar/Kingambit but dislikes Mega Gardevoir spread damage and stat drops.

decisions.rationale: Double Dark lead (Incineroar+Kingambit) blanks Prankster Encore, resists Make It Rain, and threatens Gholdengo with Kowtow Cleave. Fake Out disrupts Whimsicott Tailwind or Maushold Follow Me. Gardevoir-Mega in back as primary win condition with Pixilate Hyper Voice; Talonflame provides priority Tailwind and Fire/Flying coverage. Both back Pokémon resist Fighting for Tauros pivot. Iron Head OHKOs Ninetales-Alola if they bring it.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 won. Series 1-0. Opponent full team: Whimsicott (Prankster Focus Sash), Gholdengo (Good as Gold Wise Glasses), Blastoise-Mega (Mega Launcher), Maushold (Friend Guard), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (Intimidate Black Belt), Ninetales-Alola (Snow Warning Light Clay). Game 1 they brought Whimsicott+Gholdengo+Blastoise+Tauros; Maushold+Ninetales benched. Gholdengo Power Gem 4x threatens Talonflame. Tauros Close Combat 4x OHKOs Kingambit even at -1. Blastoise Aura Sphere 2x on Kingambit. Whimsicott Encore fails on Dark types. Focus Sash guarantees survival at full HP. Gardevoir-Mega Hyper Voice is primary win condition; Kingambit cleans late but is frail to Fighting/Fairy. Incineroar Parting Shot cycling key for debuffing. Expect possible Maushold redirection or Ninetales Aurora Veil in game 2.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand resolves before Fake Out and amplifies Gholdengo’s super-effective Power Gem into Incineroar, creating the strongest immediate chance to remove its cycling support despite likely disruption.
decisions.notebook: Incineroar commonly uses Fake Out plus Parting Shot cycling. Kingambit carries Protect and Sucker Punch, so avoid leaving Gholdengo exposed without pressure or protection. Mega Gardevoir favors Protect and repeated Hyper Voice; Talonflame favors Tailwind. Mega Blastoise answers Incineroar and Kingambit but is vulnerable to Mega Gardevoir spread damage and stat drops.

decisions.rationale: Keep Whimsicott for Prankster Tailwind, Encore, or Moonblast pressure. Bring in Blastoise as the stronger stabilizer: Mega Launcher-boosted Aura Sphere threatens Kingambit, while Water pressure answers Incineroar and it avoids relying on Tauros's lower durability.
decisions.notebook: Opponent commonly cycles Incineroar with Fake Out and Parting Shot. Kingambit has Protect and Sucker Punch; preserve pressure or protection before exposing a frail attacker. Mega Gardevoir favors Protect plus repeated Hyper Voice, Talonflame favors Tailwind, and Serperior uses Contrary Leaf Storm or Glare. Keep Whimsicott available for Prankster speed control and Encore; Mega Blastoise is a strong general answer but must respect Mega Gardevoir spread damage and stat drops.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3) flinches Whimsicott before its Prankster Tailwind (+1), denying speed control. Kowtow Cleave threatens 83.5–151.9% on Gholdengo with a strong OHKO chance. Even if Whimsicott uses Helping Hand (+6) before the flinch, boosted Power Gem does at most 81% to Incineroar and Make It Rain does at most 44% to Kingambit — both survive. Sucker Punch risks Gholdengo Protecting. This is the safest aggressive opener.

Whimsicott cannot Encore Dark types (Prankster fails vs Dark). Kowtow Cleave is a roll to OHKO Gholdengo. Friend Guard Maushold would cut that damage by 25%. Parting Shot blocked by Good as Gold. decisions.rationale: Set Tailwind before likely replacement threats and Mega Evolve Blastoise to fire Aura Sphere. Aura Sphere is 4× super effective on Kingambit and Mega Launcher makes the KO guaranteed across its legal range, while Tailwind preserves speed control against the unrevealed back line.
decisions.notebook: In future games, prioritize Mega Blastoise’s Mega Launcher Aura Sphere as the reliable answer to Kingambit. Preserve Whimsicott when possible for Prankster Tailwind and Encore; account for Prankster failing against Dark targets. Continue respecting Incineroar’s Fake Out/Parting Shot cycle and Kingambit’s Protect/Sucker Punch mind games.

Continue respecting Incineroar’s Fake Out/Parting Shot cycle and Kingambit’s Protect/Sucker Punch mind games.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 primarily because the game-2 preview plan left too much pressure on a slow Mega Blastoise and Whimsicott support core against Fake Out, Intimidate, Parting Shot, Sucker Punch, and Mega Gardevoir's spread Hyper Voice. Gholdengo was a poor lead into Kingambit and was removed immediately, while Whimsicott's Tailwind came too late to protect the team. Mega Blastoise did remove Kingambit and nearly removed Incineroar, but it was already heavily compromised before it could swing the game. Tauros and Encore briefly created value, but the four could not withstand Gardevoir's repeated spread damage. No game-1 evidence is supplied, so a specific between-game adjustment cannot be credited or blamed; the game-2 adjustment did not solve the matchup. The registered six and sets had useful tools, especially Whimsicott's Encore/Tailwind and Blastoise's Aura Sphere, but the chosen four lacked immediate speed or reliable protection. There is insufficient evidence to judge whether Gliscor, Qwilfish, Morpeko, or Meowstic-Female would have fit better, since their sets and game-1 context are unknown. Mega Blastoise was serviceable but not clearly the best Mega choice for this opponent.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, do not lead Gholdengo alongside a support-dependent partner into Kingambit and Incineroar. Bring a faster or more immediately threatening combination that can function through Fake Out and Intimidate, and preserve Whimsicott if Encore or Tailwind is central to the plan. If using Mega Blastoise, support it with protection from early spread damage and avoid relying on it to carry the game after Parting Shot and Hyper Voice; reconsider whether it is the correct Mega holder at preview. Target Gardevoir's spread-move dependence with disruption or a faster knockout route, while respecting Kingambit's Protect and Sucker Punch. Re-evaluate the four from all six only after checking the actual sets of the omitted Pokémon; current evidence does not justify claiming a specific bench choice was superior.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies and revealed facts: Incineroar has Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, and a Passho Berry; it used Fake Out repeatedly and pivots to preserve positioning. Kingambit has Protect, Sucker Punch, Kowtow Cleave, Iron Head, BlackGlasses, and Supreme Overlord; it can immediately punish exposed Gholdengo and threatens priority. Mega Gardevoir has Hyper Voice, Mystical Fire, Icy Wind, and Protect; Hyper Voice is a major sustained spread-damage plan, and it can be vulnerable to Encore after using it. Tailwind and Prankster Encore are valuable, but Whimsicott cannot be treated as disposable if they are the main speed-control and disruption tools. Gholdengo is not a safe default lead into this Incineroar/Kingambit pairing. Mega Blastoise's Aura Sphere pressures Kingambit and Incineroar, but its low speed and susceptibility to accumulated spread damage make it a poor stand-alone answer. Future preparation should prioritize immediate pressure through Fake Out, Intimidate, and Protect, plus a concrete answer to Mega Gardevoir's Hyper Voice; verify whether the omitted roster members' actual sets provide that before selecting the four.

reflections.summary: Our team's offensive synergy—Incineroar's Fake Out and Intimidate, Kingambit's Dark-type OHKO on Gholdengo, and Mega Gardevoir's Pixilate Hyper Voice—overwhelmed the opponent's slower Tailwind composition. In Game 2, we removed Gholdengo immediately, pivoted with Parting Shot, and swept with Gardevoir. The opponent's Helping Hand misplay on Gholdengo and frail support core gave us a decisive advantage. Our between-game adjustments (likely bringing the same four) proved correct, and the series was won 2-0.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, I would bring the same core (Incineroar, Kingambit, Mega Gardevoir, Talonflame) as it effectively handles their revealed threats. If they bring Maushold or Ninetales-Alola, I might consider Dragapult for speed or Taunt to disrupt Aurora Veil, but the current four are well-suited. No changes needed unless they adapt.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Whimsicott (Sash) is the only Tailwind setter and often uses Helping Hand turn 1—targeting Gholdengo failed due to Good as Gold, so they may misplay this. Gholdengo is OHKOed by Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. Blastoise-Mega (Mega Launcher) is slow and weak to Fairy. Tauros (Intimidate, BlackBelt) uses Close Combat, lowering its defenses. Maushold and Ninetales-A unrevealed but may bring Friend Guard/Aurora Veil. Win condition: Fake Out + Kowtow Cleave Gholdengo, then sweep with Mega Gardevoir Hyper Voice. Talonflame's priority Tailwind is a strong backup. Incineroar's Passho Berry was not needed; consider another item. If they bring Ninetales, include a screen remover or Taunt.
